6. 
NMRA’S Criterion for selecting a Reference Regulatory Authority 
 
To identify its reference regulatory authorities, the NMRA will use the following 
criterion: 
• Marketing authorizations: 
o Medicines: SRA, WHO prequalification, or WLA in the scope of marketing 
authorization for medicines. 
o Vaccines: Highly performing NRAs for vaccines, WHO prequalification, or 
WLA in the scope of marketing authorization for vaccines. 
• GMP inspections: 
o Medicines and vaccines: PIC/S member, WHO prequalification, or WLA in 
the scope of GMP regulatory inspection for medicines and/or vaccines. 
In addition, the NMRA will consider the availability of the minimum required information 
for reliance in a language which can be easily understood or translated. 
 
7. 
NMRA’S process for selecting a Reference Regulatory Authority 
Considering the criterion for selecting a reference regulatory authority, the Medicine 
Regulatory Division (MRD) of NMRA can propose to the Medicine Evaluation Committee 
to consider one regulatory authority as a reference regulatory authority. In addition, based 
on the same criterion, external stakeholders may request the NMRA to consider the 
addition of another reference authority. 
On the same basis, the Medicine Evaluation Committee discuss and approves the proposed 
reference authorities. 
The current list or reference regulatory authorities is published on the NMRA website. 
(www.nmra.gov.lk)  
 
8. Reliance pathways for marketing authorizations 
 
8.1 Abridged Registration for initial marketing authorisation  
 
▪ Products with marketing authorisation from one reference regulatory authority (two if API 
or fixed dose combination is new) shall be registered at NMRA within 90 days after the 
verification of the sameness of a medicinal product and taking into consideration the 
country-specific information submitted for review.  
 
▪ Chemical medicines finished products manufactured in a manufacturing site with a valid 
and relevant GMP certificate from a reference regulatory authority, and with a marketing 
authorisation in the manufacturing country and at least 3 other countries shall be registered 
at NMRA within 90 days after the verification of the sameness, bridging assessment 
depending on the scope of the GMP certificate, and taking into consideration the country-
specific information submitted for review.

1.2   Objectives

utilization of the reliance approach.

product via this pathway and serves as a supplementary document to Drug Registration 
Guidance Document (DRGD). The applicant should refer to both documents before completing 
product registration application via QUEST system.  
 
 
1.3   Scope

cell and gene therapy products (CGTPs).

decide based on the eligibility criteria stated in this guideline, which may include risk-benefit 
assessment, country priorities, public health needs, and other reasons or opportunities for reliance.

Foreword  
The Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority (PMRA) will continue to 
strengthen its regulatory systems in line with national priorities and global 

PAGE 4
iv 
 
commitments to enhance access to quality-assured, safe, and effective medical 
products. Given limited Linancial and human resources, inadequate expertise in 
pharmaceutical innovation, and evolving public health needs, regulatory reliance 
has become essential for optimizing resources, reducing duplication of efforts, and 
facilitating timely regulatory decision-making. The regulatory reliance does not 
compromise PMRA’s responsibility for ensuring product quality, safety, and 
efLicacy within the local context. 
As regulatory reliance continues to enhance regulatory efLiciency and global health 
impact, its formalization becomes more relevant to all stakeholders. Establishing 
clear guidance and procedures that support international collaboration and 
mutual reliance on regulatory decisions is crucial for sustaining these collaborative 
efforts.   
In this context, PMRA has developed these Guidelines on Regulatory Reliance for 
Marketing Authorisation of Human Medicinal Products to leverage regulatory 
work performed by competent regulatory authorities and optimize regulatory 
resources, reduce duplication of regulatory effort. This document is intended to 
guide applicants wishing to submit new applications for marketing authorisation 
through reliance pathways. The guidelines stipulate the reliance mechanisms, 
which include standard process work sharing, an abridged review pathway, 
regional reliance, and unilateral and mutual recognition.   
Through these guidelines, the Authority reafLirms its regulatory responsibility 
while recognizing the value of leveraging assessments and decisions made by 
trusted and competent regulatory authorities. Irrespective of the requirements as 
provided for in these guidelines, PMRA has the right to request additional 
information or deLine conditions that are not explicitly prescribed in this 
document that are deemed necessary for establishing the quality, safety, and 
efLicacy of the medicinal products.  PMRA retains full sovereign authority and 
responsibility for all Linal regulatory decisions taken under reliance pathways. 
It is anticipated that this document will accelerate the Authority’s decision-making 
on various regulatory functions and, in turn, ensure access and availability of 
essential medicines with the required quality standard to protect the public. PMRA 
remains committed to its mandate and will continue collaborating with national, 
regional, and international partners to promote regulatory excellence and improve 
access to essential health products in Malawi.   
3. 
Glossary of Terms  
  

PAGE 5
v 
 
The following terms are deLined for the purpose of these guidelines: -  
  
Abridged regulatory pathways   
  
Abridged regulatory pathways are regulatory procedures facilitated by the use of 
reliance, whereby the regulatory decision is solely or primarily based on the 
application of reliance. The expectation is that the use of reliance would save 
resources and shorten timelines compared to standard pathways, while 
maintaining regulatory oversight standards.  
  
Authority   
  
Refers to the Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority, or its acronym, PMRA.  
  
Equivalence of regulatory systems  
  
Implicates a strong similarity between two regulatory systems that are mutually 
established and documented through objective evidence. Equivalence can be 
established using criteria and approaches such as similarity of the regulatory 
framework and practices, adherence to the same international standards and 
guidelines, experience gained in the use of assessments for regulatory decision 
making, joint activities, and staff exchanges. It is expected that equivalent 
regulatory systems will result in similar standards and levels of regulatory 
oversight or “levels of control”.  
  
Mutual recognition agreement   
  
According to a deLinition issued by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation 
and Development (OECD), a mutual recognition agreement is a principle of 
international law whereby states party to such agreements recognize and uphold 
legal decisions taken by competent authorities in another member state. Mutual 
recognition is a process that allows conformity assessments carried out in one 
country to be recognized in another country.  
  
 
 
 
 
Recognition   
 

PAGE 6
vi 
 
Recognition differs from other forms of reliance in that recognition involves 
acceptance of another authority’s regulatory decision, whereas reliance involves 
use of another authority’s assessment to inform PMRA’s independent decision. 
  
Recognition is the routine acceptance of the regulatory decision of another 
regulator or trusted institution. Recognition indicates that evidence of conformity 
with the regulatory requirements of country A is sufLicient to meet the regulatory 
requirements of country B. Recognition should be based on evidence of conformity 
that the regulatory requirements of the reference regulatory authority are 
sufLicient to meet the regulatory requirements of the relying authority. Recognition 
may be unilateral or mutual and may, in the latter case, be the subject of a mutual 
recognition agreement.  
  
  
Reference regulatory authority (RRA)  
 
Refers to a national or regional authority, or a trusted institution such as WHO 
prequaliLication (WHO PQ), EMA, USFDA, ZAZIBONA, Africa Medicines Agency, 
whose regulatory decisions or work products are relied upon by another 
regulatory authority to inform its own decisions.  PMRA shall maintain criteria 
for the designation and periodic review of recognized Reference Regulatory 
Authorities (RRAs). 
 
  
Reliance   
  
The act whereby the regulatory authority in one jurisdiction takes into account and 
gives signiLicant weight to assessments performed by another regulatory authority 
or trusted institution, or to any other authoritative information, in reaching its own 
decision. The relying authority remains independent, responsible and accountable 
for the decisions taken, even when it relies on the decisions, assessments and 
information of others.

4. 
Introduction  
In recognition of the growing complexity of healthcare innovations, the 
globalization of pharmaceutical markets, and the need to optimize regulatory 
resources, the Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority (PMRA) has 
developed these guidelines on regulatory reliance for marketing authorisation of 
medicinal products to provide structured and transparent guidance in 
implementing reliance mechanisms in regulatory decision-making.  
International organisations, including AMA, SADC-MRH, EMA, World Health 
Organisation (WHO), and National Regulatory Authorities, have endorsed reliance 
as a best practice for accelerating the availability of health technologies to treat 
diseases. In recent years, it has become clear that many African NRAs are 
interested in implementing a risk-based approach.  PMRA may apply risk 
classiLication criteria when determining eligibility for abridged review or 
veriLication pathways, taking into account product complexity, therapeutic risk, 
public health impact, and regulatory history. 
Implementing an effective reliance mechanism can accelerate product approvals 
by reducing the timeline for the review process and minimizing duplication of 
work by using available limited resources. This will ultimately leverage regulatory 
convergence and harmonization, strengthening regional collaboration, and 
enhancing the availability of good quality, safe and efLicacious medicinal products 
to the public at large.  
  
However, despite its potential beneLits, adopting and implementing reliance 
mechanisms in most NRAs often face signiLicant challenges. These include 
diversity in regulatory levels and different regulatory requirements, difLiculty 
obtaining unredacted assessment reports, and failure to submit updated product 
dossiers from recognised regulatory agencies that had approved the product. 
Furthermore, most traditional reliance processes for abbreviated assessment, 
which were used internally by the Authority, had no clear guidance for industries 
on the requirements and procedural aspects of reliance mechanisms.  
  
To overcome these challenges, PMRA has developed this Guideline on Regulatory 
Reliance for Marketing Authorisation of Human Medicinal Products, which 
provides a structured approach enabling the applicants to comply with regulatory 
reliance pathways effectively. The guidelines outline key principles of reliance-
based evaluation pathways in which applicants should apply for the marketing

2 
 
authorisation of medicinal products. Equally, these guidelines prescribe regulatory 
review pathways of the respective applications, which include abridged review, 
veriLication of the sameness, recognition, working sharing, and joint assessment.   
  
This guideline should be read in conjunction with other guidelines, Guidelines for 
Marketing Authorisation of Medicinal Products, and other product-speciLic 
guidelines.  
5. 
Purpose   
  
This guideline is intended to guide the applicants on the requirements and review 
pathways for marketing authorisation of medicinal products through the reliance 
approach.  The guidance document will also ensure transparency, predictability, 
and efLiciency of regulatory decision-making. 
 
6. 
Legal basis   
  
These Guidelines are issued pursuant to Section 123 of the Pharmacy and 
Medicines Regulatory Authority Act No. 9 of 2019 and shall be read in conjunction 
with the applicable regulations. While PMRA may rely on regulatory decisions and 
assessment outcomes of recognised reference authorities, it retains its sovereign 
regulatory authority and responsibility for all decisions relating to the 
authorisation of medicinal products in Malawi. Accordingly, reliance does not 
constitute automatic approval or registration of a medicinal product. 
Scope  
 This guideline applies to applications for marketing authorisation of new chemical 
entities and generic medicines that have been approved or registered by AMA, 
EMA, WHO, NRAs with WHO-Maturity Level 3 (ML3)/ML4, WLAs, SADC-MRH, and 
other recognised regional harmonisation initiatives. The guideline also applies to 
variation applications for registered medicinal products. The Pharmacy and 
Medicines Regulatory Authority reserves the right to amend the list of recognised 
reference authorities from time to time, as deemed necessary.

Foreword  
The Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority (PMRA) will continue to 
strengthen its regulatory systems in line with national priorities and global 

PAGE 4
iv 
 
commitments to enhance access to quality-assured, safe, and effective medical 
products. Given limited Linancial and human resources, inadequate expertise in 
pharmaceutical innovation, and evolving public health needs, regulatory reliance 
has become essential for optimizing resources, reducing duplication of efforts, and 
facilitating timely regulatory decision-making. The regulatory reliance does not 
compromise PMRA’s responsibility for ensuring product quality, safety, and 
efLicacy within the local context. 
As regulatory reliance continues to enhance regulatory efLiciency and global health 
impact, its formalization becomes more relevant to all stakeholders. Establishing 
clear guidance and procedures that support international collaboration and 
mutual reliance on regulatory decisions is crucial for sustaining these collaborative 
efforts.   
In this context, PMRA has developed these Guidelines on Regulatory Reliance for 
Marketing Authorisation of Human Medicinal Products to leverage regulatory 
work performed by competent regulatory authorities and optimize regulatory 
resources, reduce duplication of regulatory effort. This document is intended to 
guide applicants wishing to submit new applications for marketing authorisation 
through reliance pathways. The guidelines stipulate the reliance mechanisms, 
which include standard process work sharing, an abridged review pathway, 
regional reliance, and unilateral and mutual recognition.   
Through these guidelines, the Authority reafLirms its regulatory responsibility 
while recognizing the value of leveraging assessments and decisions made by 
trusted and competent regulatory authorities. Irrespective of the requirements as 
provided for in these guidelines, PMRA has the right to request additional 
information or deLine conditions that are not explicitly prescribed in this 
document that are deemed necessary for establishing the quality, safety, and 
efLicacy of the medicinal products.  PMRA retains full sovereign authority and 
responsibility for all Linal regulatory decisions taken under reliance pathways. 
It is anticipated that this document will accelerate the Authority’s decision-making 
on various regulatory functions and, in turn, ensure access and availability of 
essential medicines with the required quality standard to protect the public. PMRA 
remains committed to its mandate and will continue collaborating with national, 
regional, and international partners to promote regulatory excellence and improve 
access to essential health products in Malawi.

Abridged regulatory pathways   
  
Abridged regulatory pathways are regulatory procedures facilitated by the use of

resources and shorten timelines compared to standard pathways, while 
maintaining regulatory oversight standards.  
  
Authority

Equivalence of regulatory systems  
  
Implicates a strong similarity between two regulatory systems that are mutually 
established and documented through objective evidence. Equivalence can be 
established using criteria and approaches such as similarity of the regulatory 
framework and practices, adherence to the same international standards and 
guidelines, experience gained in the use of assessments for regulatory decision 
making, joint activities, and staff exchanges. It is expected that equivalent 
regulatory systems will result in similar standards and levels of regulatory 
oversight or “levels of control”.  
  
Mutual recognition agreement   
  
According to a deLinition issued by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation 
and Development (OECD), a mutual recognition agreement is a principle of 
international law whereby states party to such agreements recognize and uphold 
legal decisions taken by competent authorities in another member state. Mutual 
recognition is a process that allows conformity assessments carried out in one 
country to be recognized in another country.

recognition agreement.

2.  Scope 
This guideline provides guidance to applicants and MCA regulators on the 
requirements and process for the registration/approval of medicines, (both 
innovator and multisource (generic) finished pharmaceutical products (FPPs) and 
biologicals), in The Gambia that have been approved by a recognised reference 
institution. For details on the reference institutions see section 5 and Annex I. 
By using the approach of reliance, MCA maximises the efficiency in using their own 
resources. Moreover, MCA is able to focus on value-adding activities. In addition, 
the burden of duplication of work done by reference institutions and duplication of 
work for applicants/manufacturers is reduced. 


PAGE 5
 
Guideline for Reliance on decisions, reports, or information from other national medicines regulatory 
authorities (NMRAs) or regional and international bodies 
 
 
 
MCA-GL-109, Version 1 (24 December 2021) 
Page 5/17
 
This guideline covers initial registrations/approvals and variations/post approval 
changes. 
3.  Legal basis 
This guideline is coherent with national/regional frameworks and policies. The usage 
of reliance by MCA is supported/embedded in the Part XIII, section 82 (2) of the 
Medicines and Related Products Regulations, 2020. 
4.  Assessment activities 
NMRAs have several options for organising their assessment activities.  
In addition to a full review, there exist two reliance-based approaches to organise 
the assessment activities; verification or abridged/abbreviated review/regulatory 
pathway.  
Verification is an administrative process to reach a regulatory decision, based on 
registration or authorisation by a reference institution. The NMRA formalises its 
decision by approving the product or submission and ensures the product for local 
registration and marketing. The NMRA does not undertake any further assessment 
activity on its own. This may apply to full submissions or parts thereof (see 
‘Definitions’ for details on full and partial reliance). Verification is applied where 
conformity with requirements of the reference institution is sufficient to meet the 
requirements of MCA.  
Abridged/abbreviated review is the assessment of suitability of use under local 
conditions and regulatory requirements, while relying partly or fully on prior 
assessment and inspection outcomes as well as Quality Control (QC) laboratory 
reports from the reference institution to inform the local decision (see ‘Definitions’ 
for details on abridged/abbreviated procedure). 
5.  Reference institutions

6.1.  Documentation Requirements  
The format of the documentation should correspond to the CTD in accordance with 
MCA or International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for 
Pharmaceuticals for Human Use (ICH) format/content.  
Currency of the documentation, i.e. the sameness of the contents of the application 
with the documentation available and underlying any regulatory decision of the 
reference institution is mandatory (see section 6.2). 
6.1.1.  For marketing authorisation applications 
A full dossier (CTD format) should be submitted including: 
a. Module 1, regional administrative information, adapted, following the 
contents/format/structure laid out in Annex II (“Proposed documentation for 
the abridged procedure for reference institution-approved medicine”). 
b. Module 2, summaries, complete as submitted to the reference institution. 
Note: In the case of generic medicines for which a Clinical summary is not 
available, the Clinical overview (Module 2.5) should be included. 
c. Module 3, quality documentation, as submitted to the reference institution, 
unless indicated otherwise according to the requirements of MCA. If climatic 
zone III–IV stability data are not available, the commitment and protocol 
should be provided for stability studies under the appropriate climatic 
conditions for The Gambia. Any preliminary data under the required climatic 
conditions for MCA should be provided. The stability data will be assessed by the reference 
institution, where applicable or possible. 
d. Module 4, non-clinical documentation, to be provided except for 
generic/multisource medicines in addition to summary in module 2. 


PAGE 7
 
Guideline for Reliance on decisions, reports, or information from other national medicines regulatory 
authorities (NMRAs) or regional and international bodies 
 
 
 
MCA-GL-109, Version 1 (24 December 2021) 
Page 7/17
 
e. Module 5, clinical documentation, (in addition to summary in module 2). 
For innovative medicines to be provided. 
For generic/multisource products, complete documentation on bioequivalence 
studies should be provided in the submission in line with WHO guidelines (see 
reference list (WHO. Annex 6 Multisource (generic)….) on registration 
requirements to establish interchangeability and applicable national 
regulatory requirements for MCA.  
6.1.2.  For applications for variations 
a. Module 1, adapted, following the contents/format/structure laid out in Annex 
II (“Proposed documentation for the abridged procedure for reference 
institution-approved medical products”). 
b. Module 2, complete as submitted to the reference institution. 
Note: In the case of generic medicines for which a Clinical summary is not 
available, the Clinical overview (Module 2.5) should be included. 
c. Modules 3, 4 and/or 5 as submitted to the reference institution for the 
substantiation of the applied variation. 
6.1.3.  Additional information for marketing authorisation applications as 
well as for applications for variations 
a. All review(s), assessment reports as well as inspection reports by the 
reference institution, substantiating the current authorisation status of the 
medicine, should be provided by the applicant when the submission is filed 
with MCA.  
b. Written confirmation of permission for sharing reference institution-owned 
non-public information with MCA (see Annex III). 
Note for variation applications: If the confirmation has been obtained for the 
initial marketing authorisation application with unlimited validity, the 
confirmation does not have to be renewed with the reference institution. 
Nonetheless, the written confirmation should be part of each submission.

2. 
Additional requirements for NDAs of ATPs via the abridged evaluation or verification 
routes  
2.1 
In addition to the requirements in <Guidance Notes on Registration of Pharmaceutical Products: 
New Drug Applications>, applicants are required to provide the following additional documents for 
NDAs of ATPs: 
(a) site master file(s), or equivalent, of the proposed production site(s) or facility(ies), including 
the methods, standards and conditions of the manufacture of the ATP, the manufacturing 
and quality control facilities, technical personnel, etc, for NDA of an ATP manufactured 
outside Hong Kong; 
(b) one set of prototype sales pack for each applied pack size of the product, which should 
comply with the labelling requirements specified in <Guidelines on the Labelling of 
Pharmaceutical Products> and <Guidance on Labelling Requirements of Product Code, 
Unique Donation Identifier and Unique Recipient Identifier for Advanced Therapy 
Products>, of which the label should contain product code and unique donation identifier.  
For autologous product, unique recipient identifier is also required. The coding systems 
adopted should be specified; 
(c) ICH CTD Modules 2 to 5. The specific requirements for each type of ATPs are outlined in 
the Appendices 1 to 3; 
(d) a description of the traceability system that the Registration Certificate holder intends to 
establish and maintain to ensure that the individual product and its starting and raw materials, 
including all substances coming into contact with the cells or tissues it may contain, can be 
traced through the sourcing, manufacturing, packaging, storage, transport and delivery to 
the hospital, institution or private healthcare facilities where the product is used; 
(e) strategy to evaluate long-term efficacy; 


PAGE 7

Abridged Evaluation or Verification Routes 
Page 6 
 
(f) strategy for the long-term follow-up of safety and efficacy, which should be included in the 
Risk Management Plan (“RMP”) and/or Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (“REMS”); 
and 
(g) specific expertise required to carry out the application, implantation, administration, or 
follow-up activities, and the training plan for healthcare professionals on the use, application, 
implantation, or administration procedures of these products (where necessary).

guidelines for gene, cellular and tissue-based therapies issued by reputable reference agencies such as 
European Medicines Agency and the United States Food and Drug Administration.

  the relevant Member State of the European Economic Area (in
  Latvia - to the State Agency of Medicines) (hereinafter -
  participating Member States). Data and documents indicated in the

  comply with the following requirements:
95.1. it shall be identical to the application dossier
  submitted in other referred to States;
95.2. it shall include information in accordance with Chapters
  II, III, IV, V, VI and VII of this Regulation;
95.3. it shall indicate the list of participating Member
  States, in which the registration application has been submitted
  or in which the medicinal products are registered during
  application of the application.

  registration application in the States referred to in
  Sub-paragraph 95.3 of this Regulation:
96.1. are registered, the medicinal products shall be
  registered in accordance with a mutual recognition procedure;
96.2. are not registered, but are in the process of
  registration, the medicinal products shall be registered in
  accordance with a decentralised procedure.

  procedure:
